clue.text: Plant very easy to cultivate, having only heads

indicators.note: only the heads, the opening letters, of the five words before are kept

explanation.surface: A gardener praises a plant that is easy to grow, though it only produces flower heads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'having only heads' reads as a description of the plant, but it tells you to take the first letters of 'very easy to cultivate, having'.
explanation.definitionFit: A vetch is a climbing leguminous plant of the pea family.

clue.text: Signal carrying little weight

definitions.meaning: a flare fired from a pistol, named after its inventor Very

explanation.surface: A signal that is weak and of little importance.
explanation.walkthrough: A Very light is a coloured signal flare, named after Edward Very.
explanation.definitionFit: A flare shot from a pistol is a distress beacon; something nearly weightless is extremely feathery.

clue.text: Money invested in food sent up only just warm

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means the letters read from bottom to top
money put inside the word for food, as money is invested in a venture

parts.note: diet means the food one eats
p, for penny or pence, is money

explanation.surface: Money ploughed into catering yields only a lukewarm return.
explanation.walkthrough: 'invested in' puts P inside DIET to make DIPET; 'sent up' turns that round.
explanation.definitionFit: Lukewarm, barely above cool; also used of a half-hearted response.

clue.text: War criminal concealing resentment — one to whom there's a lot coming

definitions.text: one to whom there's a lot coming

indicators.note: the criminal's name hides the word for resentment within it

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was a Nazi convicted at Nuremberg
ire is anger, resentment

explanation.surface: A war criminal hides his bitterness from someone due a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman due to inherit a fortune has a great deal coming to her.

clue.text: Aschertain what-keeps the food hot

parts.note: the printed word shows ascertain with an H lodged inside it; H is the abbreviation for hot

explanation.surface: A seemingly misspelt instruction to find out what stops dinner going cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The odd spelling is deliberate: 'Aschertain' shows 'ascertain' keeping H. Ascertain means DISCOVER, so DISCOVER keeping H gives DISH COVER.
explanation.definitionFit: A domed lid placed over a serving plate holds in the warmth of a meal.

clue.text: I'm foolish and faint-hearted, getting upset about onset of winter

indicators.note: the reversed word goes around the letter
upset in a down clue means turned over, the word read bottom to top

parts.note: timid means faint-hearted

indicators.note: the onset of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: Someone admits being a nervous fool, unsettled at the arrival of cold weather.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting upset' turns TIMID into DIMIT; 'about' puts it round W, the onset of winter. The definition is what such a person might say of themselves.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who confesses to foolishness is calling themselves a numbskull.

clue.text: The place to get a snack

definitions.text: The place to get a snack

parts.words: The place to get a snack
parts.note: read as a town name, the Kent town that gave its name to a filled bread snack

explanation.surface: A suggestion for where to buy a light meal.
explanation.walkthrough: Sandwich is a town in Kent; the snack is named after the Earl of Sandwich.
explanation.definitionFit: A Kent town shares its name with the bread snack named after its earl.

clue.text: Drug taking care of novelist

parts.note: c/o, written CO, means care of on an address
Hall Caine was a popular Victorian novelist

explanation.surface: A novelist is looked after while on drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A stimulant narcotic made from coca leaves.

clue.text: To pick on Timothy, one's in the wrong

indicators.note: the name and one's are placed inside the word for wrong

parts.note: vice means wrongdoing
one is I, so one's (one is) gives I and S

explanation.surface: Bullying Timothy, someone is acting wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one's' is read as 'one is', giving I + S.
explanation.definitionFit: To single someone out for unfair treatment, bullying them.

clue.text: Deploring the devastation inflicted on German capital

indicators.note: inflicted on places the devastation word on top of, and so before, the letter

parts.note: ruin means devastation

indicators.note: a capital letter here is the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Lamenting the destruction wreaked on Berlin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German capital' looks like Berlin but means G, the capital letter of German.
explanation.definitionFit: Regretting or lamenting something bitterly.

clue.text: Representative members of the RAF — they keep things going

parts.note: rep is the short form of a sales or union representative
the Royal Air Force is staffed by airmen

explanation.surface: A delegate and some air force personnel are credited with keeping operations running.
explanation.definitionFit: Mechanics and fitters maintain machinery so it continues working.

clue.text: Flora somewhat barbed about first part of play

parts.note: c, short for circa, means about
Act I is the opening section of a stage play

explanation.surface: A theatre critic notes that the first act contained some prickly remarks about a character called Flora.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flora' looks like a woman's name, but it means plant life; 'somewhat barbed' describes spiny desert plants.
explanation.definitionFit: Desert succulents bear spines, so as plant life they are prickly.

clue.text: Expectant mothers in court?

parts.note: read playfully as pregnant women at a royal court, it describes the attendants of a queen or princess

explanation.surface: A question about pregnant women appearing before a court of law.
explanation.walkthrough: Women 'waiting' for a baby are playfully recast as royal attendants at court.
explanation.definitionFit: Noblewomen who attend a queen are her courtly attendants; the clue puns on expectant women 'waiting'.

clue.text: Beef and other edible flesh

definitions.meaning: a game bird whose meat is eaten, unlike beef

explanation.surface: A menu listing beef and another kind of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beef' looks like the meat, but here it is the verb to complain; 'other' then plays on that false meat reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To beef means to grumble; the game bird shot on moors is also eaten as meat.

clue.text: Passed the start first, without preparation

indicators.note: first places the word for the start ahead of the other piece

parts.note: the off is the start of a race
handed means passed over

explanation.surface: A runner went past the starting line early, without getting ready.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the off' is the start of a race.
explanation.definitionFit: Done casually or impromptu, without forethought.

clue.text: Spill the beans about company cheating

indicators.note: the word for spilling the beans goes around the word for company

parts.note: to sing is slang for informing, spilling the beans
a crew is a company of workers

explanation.surface: An informer reveals what a firm has been doing in its fraudulent dealings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts SING around CREW.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for swindling or defrauding someone, taking unfair advantage.

clue.text: Drop off a new design for Pete's logo

indicators.note: redesigning the letters means arranging them anew

explanation.surface: Someone nods off while redesigning Pete's company logo.
explanation.definitionFit: To drop off is to fall asleep.

clue.text: Poisonous part of weed found in one bed amongst several

indicators.note: the bed is placed among the letters for several

parts.note: nine is taken as several
I is the Roman numeral one
a cot is a small bed

explanation.surface: Part of a toxic weed is found growing in one of several garden beds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weed' is slang for tobacco, not a garden weed.
explanation.definitionFit: The toxic alkaloid in tobacco leaves.

clue.text: Rearguard round fat American woman

indicators.note: turned round, so the word fat is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written
frail is old American slang for a woman

explanation.surface: A rearguard circles a stout American lady.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' turns FAT into TAF. FRAIL is dated US slang for a woman. The definition is cheeky: the rail runs round a ship's stern, guarding its rear.
explanation.definitionFit: This rail runs round the stern of a ship, the rear end of the vessel.

clue.text: Greed, in a strange way, predominated

indicators.note: letters put together in a strange way are rearranged

explanation.surface: Greed, oddly, won the day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is part of the fodder: GREED + IN rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruled as monarch, figuratively held sway or prevailed.

clue.text: Soldiers advanced money at one time

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, British reserve soldiers
lent means advanced as a loan

explanation.surface: Troops were given a loan in the past.
explanation.walkthrough: 'advanced money' looks like one phrase, but 'money at one time' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In the ancient world a talent was a large unit of weight and currency.

clue.text: Bill has no love for a loyal friend

parts.note: AC, for account, is a bill
hates means has no love for

explanation.surface: A man named Bill dislikes his faithful companion.
explanation.walkthrough: Achates was the faithful companion of Aeneas in Virgil's epic; his name became proverbial for a loyal friend.
explanation.definitionFit: In Virgil's Aeneid he is the faithful comrade of Aeneas, a byword for devotion.

clue.text: Film producer and actor — novelist too we hear

indicators.note: we hear signals the word sounds like a novelist's name

parts.note: H. G. Wells, author of The War of the Worlds

explanation.surface: A film-maker and performer who also wrote novels.
explanation.walkthrough: 'too' joins the parts. Orson Welles famously broadcast a radio version of Wells's The War of the Worlds.
explanation.definitionFit: Orson Welles directed and starred in Citizen Kane.

clue.text: Economise on errands his own, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone saves money by running their own errands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges ON ERRANDS HIS OWN; note 'on' is fodder, not a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to cut back spending, like a snail retracting its feelers.

clue.text: Happy, perhaps, to take part in World War four

indicators.note: taking part of the words means the letters run inside them

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased to fight in a fourth world war.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Happy' looks like an adjective, but it names one of the seven dwarfs in the Snow White tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Happy is one of Snow White's seven little companions, so an example of the type.

clue.text: Criticise cook

definitions.meaning: to cook meat in an oven

explanation.surface: Attack the chef.
explanation.definitionFit: To slate harshly; also to bake meat in an oven.

clue.text: Poet socially acceptable in Middle Eastern port

indicators.note: the letter for socially acceptable sits inside the port's name

parts.note: Aden is a port in Yemen
U means upper-class, socially acceptable

explanation.surface: A respectable poet is found in an Arabian harbour town.
explanation.walkthrough: U, from the old U and non-U distinction of upper-class usage, means socially acceptable.
explanation.definitionFit: W. H. Auden was an Anglo-American twentieth-century poet.

clue.text: Embarrassed, I returned everything to Guy

indicators.note: returned means the word for everything is turned back to front

parts.note: all means everything
to guy is to tease or ridicule

explanation.surface: Feeling awkward, someone gave everything back to a man named Guy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' looks like a name, but it is the verb to mock. 'returned' turns ALL into LLA; 'to' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling uncomfortable and self-conscious, as an awkward person does.

clue.text: Defends as fashionable a lack of colour

indicators.note: read as able to be fashioned, the letters may be shaped into a new form

explanation.surface: Someone argues that washed-out colours are stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' looks like the trend word, but it means the letters of DEFENDS AS can be fashioned anew.
explanation.definitionFit: The quality of being washed out or pale, having lost brightness.

clue.text: Found ahead in the tennis match

explanation.surface: A tennis player is ahead in the match.
explanation.definitionFit: To establish a business is to start it; leading by a set in tennis is being a set in front.
